prompt: In many countries, young people are encouraged to take a gap year between finishing high school and starting university to work or travel. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
essay:
Nowadays, the youth are motivated to take a year off to travel around the world or enter the workplace before going to university. I firmly believe that work can help young people choose a subject, and travel can help them learn about the world.

The young generation is motivated to take a gap year to work in distinct places. Trying new workplaces at a young age helps to clarify which degree is the most appropriate. Without gaining

working experience, the students may not know their abilities, leading to future confusion in a

career path. For instance, the student who had worked as a shop assistant gained knowledge of

selling goods by communicating with customers, as a result, understood his management skills and  entered a business subject at an

educational institution.

Other young individuals are inspired to spend a year travelling. Gaining experience through meeting locals, researching new cultures and spots aids in understanding which qualifications students would like to study. A one-year journey learns how to live on one’s own, saves money, get over difficult situations and grows a strong personality.  Also, a long-term journey is required to be well-planned to avoid wasting time and resources. For example, students who have explored the world are more likely to choose a tourism field. However, some families can't afford to pay for a long journey, so instead they can have short trips. This means a travel field could be less commonly chosen, while work is a lower-cost gap-year choice.

In conclusion, it is often the case that parents inspire their kids to postpone entering university to work or to travel. I am in favour that work helps with a job choice, while travel helps people grow and learn about other places.
